content:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiered adapter surface between model profile metadata and runtime selection. intent: separate perf/compactness tiers from quality explainability. tradeoffs below.

maria: Can you sketch how this differs from existing profiles/adapters?

sam: Short sketch: 1) profile descriptor (static): accepted bitwidths, fallback order, required calib artifacts. 2) adapter chain (runtime): small pluggable transforms mapping request -> chosen profile + per-request overrides (e.g., headwise). 3) contracts: quality floor + telemetry hooks for post-hoc audits.

kevin: My worry is combination explosion = observability debt. how do we keep selection debuggable?

sam: Two mitigations: 1) deterministic selection keys logged per request (profile_id, adapter_version, selector_reason). 2) runtime writes a canonical fingerprint for applied chain (hash of canonicalized adapter list + params). makes offline grouping easy.

li: Example config?

sam: tiny example:

```
profile: "redwood/fp8-compact-v2"
adapters:
  - name: "default-tier"
    allowed_bits: [8,4]
    fallback: ["fp8-saturated","int8-safe"]
  - name: "explain-hint"
    override_for: { prompt_tags: ["code","finance"] }
    min_quality: 0.94
```

maria: How enforce min_quality? is that an eval metric attached to the profile?

sam: yes. profiles carry anchor evals (small prompt sets + expected metrics). runtime runs shadow sampling on a fraction of traffic; if degradation > threshold adapters are disabled for that endpoint.

jordan: customer pinning? Customers will often pin a profile. we should allow it but surface rollbacks to ops.

sam: customer_pin overrides selection but we add a telemetry warning flag and enable a soft-fallback toggle for emergency unpin by ops.

kevin: adapters+profiles need versioning. semver-ish metadata? how to handle compat?

li: api ergonomics: should SDKs surface adapters or only profiles? simpler to expose only profiles.

sam: propose external API exposes only profiles; adapter surface internal to runtime/ops console. reduces user complexity.

maria: another tradeoff: compact profiles (4-bit) can cause late-token degradation — small evals miss that. need longctx regression checks in canaries.

jordan: add canary plan: shadow runs with replayed session tails, tokenwise divergence metrics, require Nk requests to pass. if drift > X reject.

kevin: runtime fallback latency: selecting int8 fallback might break latency SLO. need selection policy with latency budget.

sam: add selection_policy config:

```
selection_policy:
  latency_budget_ms: 120
  quality_floor: 0.90
  prefer_lower_cost: true
```

li: ownership? eng-runtime implements adapter surface, eng-ml owns profile heuristics, eng-sre defines canary gate thresholds?

maria: sounds right. ops needs UI to show per-request fingerprint + selector reason.

ops-bot: created canary pipeline ticket (#canary-pipelines/quant-profiles) :white_check_mark:

kevin: migrations: when adapter semantics change, annotate compatibility breaks. add compat_level and automated migration checker that runs synthetic prompts.

sam: agreed. compat metadata = { compat_level: int, migration_notes: url }. registry enforces compat_level bump for breaking changes and runs migration tests.

jordan: actionable. next steps?

sam: i'll draft an RFC with: profile/adapters proto schema, logging contract, canary harness plan, minimal ui mock. target: RFC by end of week.

maria: i'll add eval prompts (finance, code, longform, longctx stress) to RFC.

li: i'll sync with eng-runtime on selection API and perf hooks.

kevin: i'll prototype the fingerprint format + small cli to decode it.

jordan: ops will prepare canary runbooks and thresholds.

sam: quick note: keep design discussion here; implementation specifics go in RFC. :thumbsup:
